qs.q: Which type of image is called a 1-bit monochrome image since it contains no color?
e: In a binary image each pixel is represented by exactly one bit (0 = black, 1 = white).
Because one bit can only encode two states, no gray levels or colors exist, so it is called a 1-bit monochrome image.
A gray image uses 8 bits per pixel (0-255) and an RGB image uses 24 bits per pixel, so they are not 1-bit images.
CMY images are also color images, so they need more than one bit per pixel.

qs.q: By reducing the sound wave sample rate, the amount of data you need to store is ____.
e: To store sound digitally, the voltage of the analog wave is sampled at frequent intervals (typically 48 kHz, i.e. 48,000 samples per second).
Each sample is stored as a binary code (typically 16 or 32 bits).
Data size = number of samples x bits per sample. Fewer samples per second means fewer codes to store, so the data is reduced.
The trade-off is lower sound quality, because the digital approximation follows the wave less closely.

qs.q: A color image (24 bits per pixel) supports $256 \times 256 \times 256$ possible combined colors.
e: In a color image each pixel is represented by 24 bits, made of three values: Red, Green and Blue.
Each of the three values uses 8 bits, so it has 256 possible levels.
Total combinations = 256 x 256 x 256 = $2^{24}$ = 16,777,216 possible colors, so the statement is True.

qs.q: When a sound wave is stored digitally, the voltage samples are stored as a binary code, typically 16 or 32 bits per sample. This step is called ____.
e: Storing a sound wave digitally has two steps.
Sampling: the voltage is measured at frequent intervals, typically 48 kHz (48,000 times per second).
Decoding (as named in the lecture): each sample is stored as a binary code, typically 16 or 32 bits per sample.
Frequency (the pitch of the tone) and amplitude (the loudness) are properties of the wave itself, not storage steps.

qs.q: An image on a seven-segment display can be represented by ____ bits.
e: Image representation depends on what the output device can display.
A seven-segment display has 7 segments (a to g), and each segment is either ON (1) or OFF (0).
So one bit per segment is enough: 7 bits. Example: digit 0 = 1111110, digit 1 = 0110000.

qs.q: In a ____ image, a pixel is represented by one bit.
e: Raster images store pixels, and the pixel size depends on the image type.
Binary image: 1 bit per pixel. Gray image: 8 bits per pixel (values 0-255). Color (RGB) image: 24 bits per pixel.
Therefore the image type that uses one bit per pixel is the binary image.

qs.q: A ____ is a collection of four bits, which is a particularly interesting data structure for hexadecimal numbers.
e: Data representation units: bit = 1 binary digit, nibble = 4 bits, byte = 8 bits (2 nibbles), word = larger group (e.g. 16 bits = 2 bytes).
A nibble is 4 bits and each hexadecimal digit corresponds to exactly one nibble (0000 to 1111 = 0 to F).
That is why nibbles are convenient for hexadecimal numbers.
